household.title: Small basket, with square base and round top. Design in black.
Bag - String handbag, with plaited " root" rings for string to run through
Dish - Wooden dish, with carved illustration and black and white decoration round the brim

Bag - Quadrangular string bag of fibre, with a design of six fields each consisting of four black stripes. Attached to the top are 16 cane loops which form the drawstring mechanism and from where the plant fibre string runs down to the right and left bottom corners of the bag. The string loops on either side and is worn over the shoulders, with the bag worn on the back.

Bag - String bag. The actual square bag is made of fibre coloured with five fields consisting of five black stripes each. Attached to the top are 14 loops made of cane which hold the plant fibre string that runs down to the right and left bottom corners of the bag. The string loops on either side and is worn over the shoulders, with the bag worn on the back. When the string is pulled through the cane rings the top of the bag closes.

Cup - Wooden double cup depicting carved human figures, an unidentified animal and geometric designs. Cups separated by centralstru, which extends at ends, potentially used as a handle. The shape of the cups can be described as quadrangular, while the four sides are almost bent in a sickle shape. Two corners/angles of the cups are sharp and two are flattened. Condition fair: One crack on one handle, two holes on the other one.

Wooden double cup, carved with a four-headed snake design. A handle with incised rhombs in the snake’s body connects the two cups. A projection at each side of the cups is carved with snake’s heads. The shape of the cups can be described as quadrangular, while the four sides are almost bent in a sickle shape and the four corners are flattened.
Bowl - Circular wooden bowl carved with human figures hunting deer -like animals on the rim and the flat base.

Box - Rectangular box with lid secured by metal hinges. The lid is carved what appears to be a hunting scene, with human figures and deer-like animals in relief, which are surrounded by two double-headed snakes. Bands of triangles are carved along the four corners of the base.

Platter - Wooden dish/platter carved with human figures, a single face and a deer-like animal with inlaid black and white triangular decoration around the rim. A projection on the rim, probaly used as a handle, forms a carved human figure wearing a hat, shown from the waist. Facing this are two human faces carved in the rim, turned towards each other. two men are carrying the deer.
Ladle - A wooden carved ladle with incisions of human figures on the bowl. The handle shows three human figures, one of them is encased by a snake up to the shoulder and another one is crouching.
Wooden comb, incised and carved decoration of trophy heads

Tungpaw(?). Woman’s long-sleeved, wrap dress or robe of black velvet, lined with cotton or synthetic black fabric; open to side with buttons along top right. Round collar with orange zigzag beaded decoration and pink cotton lining. Garment edges on both sides decorated with band of geometric motifs in orange, yellow, green, white and black beads and further row of stitched aluminium discs with aluminium chain above. Centre and reverse front decorated with black and blue velvet appliquéd beaded butterfly at centre, with anthropomorphic figures flanked by snakes, above and below. Cuffs and right side of chest appliquéd with velvet panels of repeated beaded anthropomorphic figures with aluminium discs and chain below.

Vayavay; kun. Woman’s skirt of yellow cotton cloth partly open at one side, and fastened with a loop and strap at the waist. Panel of black velvet appliquéd to lower edge and decorated with butterflies, snakes and anthropomorphic faces, wearing ovoid linear headdresses, in orange, green, yellow, white and blue glass beads, intersected by sequins. Row of aluminium discs stitched along top edge of panel; band of repeated short linear beads along bottom edge of panel, which is further strung with metal bells on small beaded loops.

Tsatsavu. Pair of short, rectangular, women’s leggings. Made of black velvet with green synthetic band stitched along top, which extends to form ties either side. Further panel of black velvet appliquéd to front lower edge, decorated with repeated anthropomorphic faces, wearing ovoid linear headdresses, in orange, green, yellow, white and blue glass beads, intersected by sequins. Row of aluminium discs stitched along top edge of panel; band of beaded diamond motifs along bottom edge of panel.

Gamuts. Woman’s headdress of black velvet decorated with pig or boar tusks. Central row of cowrie shells stitched along front with bands of pink, blue, green and yellow glass beads above and below, arranged into geometric patterns. Decorative metal chain stitched along front top and bottom. At front centre, three groups of outward pointing tusks: four tusks at centre, and three tusks in groups either side. Tusks wrapped in vertical black velvet bands with rows of red, yellow, green and white beads. Two mustard-yellow synthetic ties either side with further tassels below, stitched on reverse, in green, black, blue, mustard and red. Reverse also black velvet.

Ibuk. Round neck, long sleeved jacket of blue velvet, decorated with anthropomorphic and zoomorphic figures in orange, yellow, green and white glass beads. Centre front appliquéd with black velvet panels with rows of beaded anthropomorphic heads, arms raised; seven shell buttons with yellow, red and green plaited synthetic wool loops. Semicircular appliqué collar on reverse with three beaded snake-like figures intersected by beaded faces and enclosed by geometric bands containing sequins; aluminium chain stitched below collar. Large appliqué tiger, two butterflies and further winged figure at centre reverse. Panels of beaded anthropomorphic figures along bottom edge with snake motifs either side. Appliqué sleeve panels depict snake-like figure, butterfly and snake; cuff panels of foliate motifs containing sequins with geometric bands above and below. Metal discs stitched along beadwork edges. Blue synthetic cloth lining.

Gamuts. Man’s headdress of black velvet, glass beads, pig or boar skin and tusks. Body of headdress consists of sturdy upright band wrapped in velvet, reverse secured with plaited ties in red, yellow and green synthetic wool. Lower exterior decorated with band of cowrie shells, enclosed top and bottom with bands of muted orange and green beads; small repeated triangles of dark green beads run along top band. Upper front and sides covered with pig or boar skin with coarse brown upright hair; pig or boar tail extends upright from centre front. Circular ornament at centre front of muted green and orange beads in alternating triangular pattern, encircled by eleven large tusks, with conus shell disc at centre; further small multicoloured bead at centre of conus disc.

Gamuts. Man’s headdress of red velvet decorated with beads and pig or boar tusks. Body of headdress consists of sturdy upright band, raised at front. Reverse secured with plaited and woven ties in red, yellow and green synthetic wool. Exterior sides decorated with beads in muted orange, greens and blue arranged geometrically with a central band of diamond motifs. Two circular, concentric layers of same beads arranged in chevrons, encircled by tusk tips (one missing), at front; ground conus shell disc with multicoloured bead attached to centre. Aluminium chain stitched along top and bottom of beaded front and sides.

Cloth - Piece of dark blue cloth, with embroidery in yellow, red and green. The pattern is called " Tomoan"

Black velvet, crescent-shaped woman’s collar, backed with floral patterned cloth. Front decorated at centre and either side with anthropomorphic faces wearing ovoid linear headdresses, intersected by butterflies and snakes in yellow, orange, green and white glass beads. Sequins and small bead crosses with sequins at centre dispersed between main figures. Bands at top and bottom of repeated groups of beads arranged in triangles. Lower edge stitched with sequins and aluminium chain, which is strung with aluminium plaques, decorated with leaves and flowers, spade-shaped ornaments and small metal bells. Four cowrie shells stitched on front centre and sides. Press studs along one top edge with short cream fabric ties on top interior edge.

Two circular beads at both ends hold the cotton threads together; secured with a plaited strap, made of blue and white cotton thread.Possibly missing several beads (orange) on one thread.

Necklace - Woman’s necklace. Three rows of orange; yellow/green and multi-coloured disc-shaped glass beads, with rectangular shell spacers, arranged in multiple groups of 6 or 7 beads, alternating with single beads. The central section consists of multi-coloured beads. Secured with black and white plaited threads.

other.title: Tjevet. Wide, man’s kilt of black synthetic fibre with beaded waistband. Front of waistband decorated with band of anthropomorphic faces in orange, green, yellow and red glass beads; small aluminium discs between each face and three rows of beads below in purple, black and green. Two larger anthropomorphic faces wearing ovoid headdresses set at centre thirds. Simple machine stitched hem along kilt bottom and short ties either side of waistband.

Valan. Man’s sash of red cotton with central row of white plastic discs, each separated by two flower-shaped sequins. Plaited band of synthetic wool in yellow, green and red strung along centre over white discs. Band of small blue, orange, yellow, green and white beads arranged in triangular or chevron motif along top and bottom of sash, enclosed by aluminium chains, which extend as tassels at one end, and loop at other. Tassel end also decorated with two tassels of coloured beads terminating in metal bells. Reverse lined with blue synthetic fleece and blue cloth, possibly cotton.
